chunks: From him, from these three, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who sells goods to a group, bringing them this batch, that pair of batches, and this triple batch, with some being superior to others. Then a man comes to him and says, 'Sell them to me as a single lot.' He said, 'I do not like that.'

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: Superior, better in quality or value
key_terms.الْجُمْلَة: A batch, lot, or collective sum of goods
key_terms.مَا يُعْجِبُنِي: I do not like (a common phrase in hadith indicating disapproval or a specific legal stance)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling mixed-quality goods as a single lot in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expresses disapproval of selling mixed-quality goods as a single undifferentiated lot, a practice common among brokers (*simsar*) to obscure value disparities. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic concern with *gharar* (uncertainty) and fairness, ensuring that buyers are not misled by the aggregation of superior and inferior items into one opaque price. It serves as a foundational precedent for modern commercial ethics regarding transparency in bulk sales and asset valuation.
